title: What they said at the time

clips.q: We’re confident that it’s going to be even more successful than it is now.
We feel that that is an absolutely magnificent figure.
clips.who: **Brian Dyson**, on 55% of the country trying the new Coke, UPI, Jun 10, 1985[^5]

clips.q: Thousands of dedicated Coca-Cola consumers have told us they still want the original taste as an option. We have listened and we are taking action to satisfy their request.
We’re not surprised to hear Coke is reintroducing its old formula because quite clearly the new formula was universally hated.
We’re elated that the American consumer can have a choice and get the Old Coca-Cola back.
clips.who: **Gay Mullins**, Old Cola Drinkers of America, UPI, Jul 10, 1985[^6]

clips.q: It all kind of worked out. You know, serendipity has a lot to do with life.
clips.who: **Donald Keough**, at Coca-Cola’s centennial, UPI, May 8, 1986[^9]

clips.q: We set out to change the dynamics of sugar colas in the United States, and we did exactly that -- albeit not in the way we had planned.
clips.who: **Roberto Goizueta**, 1995, as quoted in Coca-Cola’s published history[^1]

clips.q: They didn’t ask the critical question of Coke users: Do you want a new Coke?
clips.who: **Sam Craig**, professor of marketing, New York University, msnbc.com, Apr 22, 2005[^17]

clips.q: The reason for being, for classic as a descriptor, has all but disappeared.
clips.who: **Scott Williamson**, Coca-Cola spokesman, the Associated Press, Jan 30, 2009[^19]
